newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish government favours bourse-OM merger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish government favours bourse-OM merger.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minster Erik Asbrink on Monday backed a Central Bank recommendation to merge the Stockholm Stock Exchange and the OM derivatives and futures exchange as a worthwhile step.

"An increased technical integration between, among others, market places and clearing organisations is a necessary condition for a well functioning Swedish infrastructure," Asbrink said in a statement.
"The aim to bring OM and the bourse closer to each other is therefore a step in the right direction," he added.
The Finance Ministry would shortly present a proposal to increase surveillance of bourse operations, Asbrink said.
"The proposal aims to guarantee that confidence in the Swedish bourse remains, despite any changes to the current structure," he said.
He also called for negotiations on securities registrar VPC between the state, which holds a 50 percent stake in the company, and other owners.
"Negotiations should start with other owners about the company's future operations and how they could be coordinated with, among others, marketplaces," he said.
Asbrink will propose that deputy central bank governor Stefan Ingves should represent the state in these negotiations.
Ingves said earlier on Monday that he was positive to a merger between the bourse and OM, but he did not think the state's share in VPC should be part of merger talks.
